tasks.title: Treatment design for different contaminant classes
tasks.prompt: Two water samples both appear clear. Sample A has high electrical conductivity; sample B has low conductivity but a separate microbial test is positive. Choose treatment sequences for each that meet both dissolved-ion and microbial goals, and explain why sediment filtration alone or conductivity alone cannot certify either sample.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: High conductivity in A supports appreciable mobile ions but does not identify every solute; dissolved-ion reduction may require validated desalination (e.g., reverse osmosis or distillation) and separate microbiological assurance. Low conductivity in B does not exclude microorganisms, so validated disinfection and microbial retesting are needed. Ordinary sediment filtration reduces many suspended particles but does not reliably remove dissolved salts or all pathogens. The performance goals must be measured independently using solute and microbial tests, not one visual or conductivity reading.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Choose models/treatments based on contaminant class.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate measured clarity/conductivity to species hypotheses.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Design separate intervention and verification stages.
factor_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: Low conductivity can hide microbes; visual clarity is misleading.

tasks.title: Regional acid rain and contradictory source attribution
tasks.prompt: A mountain monitoring station records repeated rain pH below its historical baseline, higher sulfate and nitrate deposition, and a strong prevailing wind from a distant industrial region. Local traffic is low. After a local facility closes, one month of readings remains acidic. One student asserts 'the distant factory must be the sole cause'; another asserts 'acid rain continuing after the local facility closed proves all industrial emissions are irrelevant'. Evaluate both claims, build a chemical transport/deposition account with at least two alternative contributions, and design a before/after plus upwind/downwind measurement strategy that can reject a false attribution.
tasks.post_commit_worked_answer: Neither universal claim follows. Combustion-derived SO₂/NOₓ can undergo atmospheric oxidation and form acidic species transported long distances; sulfate/nitrate evidence and wind support a regional contribution but do not identify a unique factory. Natural background acidity from CO₂, regional mixed sources, different meteorology, deposition lags, and changing emissions are alternatives. Persistence after a local closure does not disprove a distant contribution or residual regional emissions. Compare matched intervals and conditions, multiple sites and wind trajectories, source-specific emission inventories, precipitation ionic composition, and instrument calibration. An appropriately cautious inference is that the record is consistent with transported sulfur/nitrogen pollutants but underdetermined for sole-source responsibility.
tasks.protected_work: Choose the scientific model and independently reconcile at least two representations or observations, including a credible alternative or boundary.

factor_evidence.concept_model_selection: Compare competing source and transport mechanisms.
factor_evidence.representation_translation: Translate pH/ion/wind observations to a source–reaction–deposition chain.
factor_evidence.reasoning_chain_length: Reconcile historical baseline and closure-era data across steps.
factor_evidence.trap_exception_sensitivity: Both familiar causal shortcuts are invalid and require discriminating controls.
